notes: Cliff cream (#EFE4D0) as the mid, lavender shadow, warm cream lit. gradientBase/gradientHeight are OBJECT space and this geometry is unit-sized: metre-scale values here saturate the sweep to a constant and switch the vertical gradient off entirely, which is how every instanced asset in the greybox lost it. Brush params re-authored once the LOD ladder gained a floor (see `lod` in painterly.ts): with `.max(0)` clamping the ladder at the authored world scale, a 5 m mark period on a 10 m block meant ZERO variation across a 200 px facet, and a 60x60 patch inside the nearest cliff face in lagoon-morning.png measured luma std 0.009 against 0.096 in the cliff interior of refs/painterly/cliffs-tohad.jpg. The terrain's own brushStrength (meadow 1.45) was carrying the structure gate while every instanced prop rode for free. rampSoftness widened from a near-cel width: on a facet whose N.L is almost constant, a half-width that tight lets the micro-relief flip the terminator back and forth within a pixel or two, and the result is the ragged navy/cream boundary with magenta-cyan chromatic fringing visible down the shaded faces in shots/lagoon-morning.png. A wider step turns the same signal into a gradient the resolve and the chromatic aberration can both survive.
